newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Striking Venezuelan doctors probed in 10 deaths.
newsitem.headline: Striking Venezuelan doctors probed in 10 deaths.

text.p: Venezuelan authorities, trying to end a week-old public doctors' strike, said on Friday they had ordered an investigation into the deaths of 10 patients who died for apparent lack of adequate medical attention.
National Public Prosecutor Ivan Dario Badell told reporters some of the 10 reported cases could be of "homicide by negligence ... as stated in the Penal Code" and threatened legal action.

Union delegates of Venezuela's 27,000 public doctors, who are demanding a substantial pay increase, have blamed the government's intransigence for health hazards arising at some of the country's 300 public hospitals and 6,000 clinics.

"We've been discussing this (salary) problem with the government for the past 14 months. We're being denied decent wages," Juan Bautista Diaz, a member of the Federation of Venezuelan Doctors (FMV) executive committee, told Reuters.
He said Venezuelan doctors' salary levels, with a minimum monthly wage of $126, lagged far behind their colleagues in other Latin American countries.
After initially asking for a $1,000 minimum salary, he said the FMV would now settle for $735 (330,000 bolivars).
The government has said it will not negotiate with the striking doctors until they returned to work. Some government officials have called the strikers criminals.
Military doctors and medical students are staffing emergency wards and the most acute cases are sent to military hospitals. Women give birth sometimes with only the help of nurses.
Doctors say the Health Ministry's budget is too small and has left hospitals without proper equipment and adequate supplies as basic as needles and gauze.
